summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of severe osteoporosis, prior CABG, and chronic back pain was admitted after developing worsening back pain at home. Imaging revealed a new subacute T12 vertebral compression fracture, initially concerning for malignancy. A second radiology review and spine surgery evaluation confirmed the fracture was due to osteoporosis, not cancer, and no surgical intervention was needed. She was managed with an LSO brace, pain control including tramadol, and continued home medications. During her stay, she developed a urinary tract infection treated with a short course of ciprofloxacin. Chronic thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and macrocytic anemia were noted, with improvement in counts after vitamin supplementation. Malnutrition was addressed with nutritional support. She had one episode of stool incontinence but refused rectal exam; neurologic exam remained stable. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with plans for outpatient follow-up in endocrinology and primary care for osteoporosis management, iron studies, and blood count monitoring.
problems: Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter for fracture
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
